correctness.rationale: For every N>=3 and real flux mod 2*pi, exact Fourier eigenvalues split into simple, one-fixed-plus-pairs, two-fixed-plus-pairs, or all-paired energies according to flux and parity. Every eigenspace has nonzero projection from the localized seed, so its distinct-energy count is the Krylov dimension. Finite Cesaro dephasing gives an equal-weight identity in the generic and even half-flux cases. At zero flux an explicit reflection-symmetric shell basis is the ordered Lanczos basis; two finite cosine sums give all averaged shell populations, and rational sums yield all four stated means. Odd half flux is gauge-equivalent to negative zero-flux coupling. Continuity at fixed time follows by stable first d_* Gram-Schmidt vectors and vanishing amplitudes along the extra vectors. Standalone spectral polynomial reconstruction and independent finite-time quadrature passed 1300 checks; infinite and all-size conclusions rest on the analytic proof. No invalid nondegenerate-eigenvalue formula is applied at an exceptional flux.

value.rationale: A complete uniform-cycle benchmark for Krylov spread complexity under gauge flux is a mathematically natural observable/parameter problem motivated by the original quantum-walk complexity framework. The exact flux discontinuity grows linearly with N and survives every nonzero detuning; the different even half-flux and odd half-flux branches reflect distinct cyclic-space ranks and symmetry. The noncommutation of finite-time and infinite-time flux limits is a robust conceptual boundary. The result is neither an arbitrary finite test nor merely a substitution into a known graph table, and the all-size classification is exactly proved.
